title: Retry policy
description: Re-attempts a failed dispatch with exponential backoff. A domain failure is retried; a cancellation and a contract violation are not — the latter is a property of the manifest and would fail identically every time.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: Re-attempts after the first try. 0 disables retrying.

initialDelay.title: Initial delay
initialDelay.description: How long to wait before the first re-attempt, at least zero: a duration (`250ms`, `2s`) or an integer number of milliseconds. 250ms when omitted.

factor.title: Factor
factor.description: Multiplier applied to the delay after each re-attempt.

maxDelay.title: Max delay
maxDelay.description: Ceiling on the delay between re-attempts, at least zero: a duration (`30s`) or an integer number of milliseconds. 32s when omitted.

jitter.title: Jitter
jitter.description: `full` picks each delay uniformly from [0, delay], which is what stops work that failed together from re-attempting together.

nonRetryable.title: Non-retryable codes
nonRetryable.description: Error codes that end the loop immediately instead of consuming the budget. The built-in exclusions are the ones decidable without judgement — a cancellation, and the kernel's verdicts on the shape of the call; whether a DOMAIN failure is worth re-attempting only the author knows, and without this every terminal one is retried to exhaustion — for a non-idempotent target, N extra attempts at a side effect.

retryAfter.title: Retry after
retryAfter.description: CEL over the failure just caught (`error`): a duration replaces the computed backoff before the next re-attempt, and null keeps it. How a failure that says when to come back — a rate limit's reset time in its data — is waited out exactly. Waited as stated, with no jitter, and capped by `maxDelay`. `error` exists only where the policy is evaluated per failure; where the resource holding it resolves its fields once, when it is created, it is a fixed wait.

error.description: The failure the re-attempt is deciding about.

code.description: Structured error code; INTERNAL_ERROR for a failure that carries none.

data.description: Structured payload the failure carries, else null.

delay.title: Delay
delay.description: DEPRECATED — write `initialDelay`, which takes a duration. A duration string (`250ms`, `1s`) read as `initialDelay` when that is absent. The pattern is what makes a typo a `telo check` failure instead of a silently different backoff.
